name: WATERS, Larissa Joy

headline.note: Official parliamentary and contemporary sources establish legal research at the Queensland Land and Resources Tribunal in 2000-01, Freehills legal work in 2001-02 and community environmental-law employment at EDO Queensland from April 2002 until the Senate term began in 2011. Exact appointment boundaries, hours and leave are not published, so none of these professional roles is assumed full-time. EDO employment is nonprofit and elected office is excluded; no headline total is calculable.

career_spells.employer: Griffith University and College of Law, New South Wales
career_spells.role: Bachelor of Science, Bachelor of Laws and Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice student
career_spells.evidence_note: The Parliamentary Handbook records the three qualifications. Study commencement and completion dates are not supplied; the legal-employment chronology begins in 2000.

Official parliamentary and ABC profiles give legal-research service at the Queensland Land and Resources Tribunal from 2000 to 2001. Exact appointment and cessation dates, hours and leave are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Public control and the year interval are supported, but the evidence required for a full-time duration is absent.

career_spells.evidence_note: The Parliamentary Handbook gives 2001-02 legal work at Freehills. A contemporary professional journal says Waters worked in the Brisbane office of a national law firm before joining EDO Queensland in April 2002. Exact start, cessation, hours and leave are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but exact dates and full-time evidence are incomplete.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official Parliamentary Handbook records community environmental-law work from 2002 to 2011. A contemporary professional journal identifies an April 2002 start at EDO Queensland, and Waters has described almost a decade on an award wage there. The exact cessation, hours and leave are not published; 30 June 2011 is used only as the day before her Senate term began, not as a proved payroll endpoint.
career_spells.counting_note: EDO Queensland was a community legal centre/nonprofit, so the employment is reported separately and excluded from public/private headline totals.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official records show Waters' first Senate term began on 1 July 2011 and ended with her resignation on 18 July 2017 after discovering Canadian citizenship.

career_spells.role: Party and candidate-support work following Senate resignation; paid status unknown
career_spells.evidence_note: On resigning, Waters said she would work with the party, state candidates, members and supporters; she later sought preselection and returned via a casual vacancy. Sources reviewed do not identify an employer, employment contract, remuneration, hours or other work during the nearly 14-month interval.
career_spells.counting_note: Party work is excluded; this spell preserves the unresolved interval without assuming paid employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: Queensland parliamentary and federal records show Waters was appointed to the casual vacancy and sworn into the Senate on 10 September 2018. Her September 2026 resignation from Greens leadership and announced medical leave do not end the underlying Senate office.

research_notes: Obtain exact Griffith University and College of Law study dates and any employment overlap.
Obtain exact appointment/cessation, hours and leave for the Land and Resources Tribunal and identify whether the legal-research role was a public-service appointment or another arrangement.
Obtain Freehills exact commencement and April 2002 cessation, hours and leave.
Obtain EDO Queensland payroll cessation, hours, leave and any internal title changes; 30 June 2011 is only an outer bound from the Senate term.
Resolve whether Waters had paid party employment or other paid work during 18 July 2017 to 10 September 2018; current evidence establishes party activity but not employment.
Do not treat the September 2026 resignation from Greens leadership or announced medical leave as an end to elected office unless official Senate service records later show a vacancy.
